newsitem.title: USA: Elections officials certify Miami arena ballot.
newsitem.headline: Elections officials certify Miami arena ballot.

text.p: Florida's Dade County will hold a referendum on whether to use tax money to build a $165 million arena for the Miami Heat, county Elections Supervisor David Leahy said Monday.

Leahy's office certified that opponents of the plan had collected enough voter signatures to put the arena question on the Nov 5 ballot. Wording of the ballot question was still being drafted by the county attorney, Leahy said.
"The county commission still has to pass a resolution calling the election. That will contain the wording," Leahy said.

The Metro-Dade County Commission has already approved a plan calling for the Miami Sports & Exhibition Authority to issue revenue bonds to finance the project. The Heat has agreed to pay $50 million and the rest of the debt service is to be paid from a hotel bed tax and a sales tax rebate.

Attorney Dan Paul led the effort to force a referendum, saying the expenditure of tax money would primarily benefit a private, for-profit organization. Paul also opposed the arena site, on public park land purchased with proceeds from a previous bond issue.
The referendum requires only a simple majority of 50 percent of the votes cast, plus one, Leahy said.
Exit polls conducted during last week's countywide mayoral race show 76 percent of voters opposed the arena project and 24 percent favored it.

Heat executives criticized the poll results, saying the question was worded misleadingly. They have begun an advertising campaign telling voters that most of the cost would be borne by visitors who pay the existing hotel tax, and not by residents.

Rejection of the arena plan could jeopardize expansion plans at the adjacent Port of Miami. The new arena is part of a Maritime Park project that includes four new cruise ship terminals, parking garages and possibly a museum and retail space.
